issue.title: Host header is being set incorrectly, by appending port unnecessarily

repository.name: cypress
repository.description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

issue.body:
@bahmutov Related to #215.

This is actually a bug in the underlying `request` library we use to issue HTTP requests. I've opened an issue here: https://github.com/request/request/issues/2372

`request` is appending the `port` to the `Host` header which causes `zeit.co` to return a 404 (like all reverse proxies likely will). That's because `port` should only be appended to the `Host` header when its not `80` or `443`.

You can simulate exactly what `request` is doing under the hood via `curl`.

``` bash
## this will return 404
curl -I https://todomvc-express.bahmutov.com:443/app.css --header 'Host: todomvc-express.bahmutov.com:443'
```

``` bash
## this will return 200
curl -I https://todomvc-express.bahmutov.com:443/app.css --header 'Host: todomvc-express.bahmutov.com'
```

After splunking through `request's` code I see that if we were to parse out the url ourselves instead of providing as a string, it would work correctly. So we'll do that until they issue a fix.

body:
Both of the issues discussed here are due to #222.

Closing in favor of that issue.

Also I would probably open an issue with `zeit.co` as well because their reverse proxy should probably take this into account.

This will be fixed in `cypress` but there over _16 million_ downloads of the `request` module per month.

Additionally - it seems to only happen if you _include_ the port in the url.

This will fail:

```
request("https://todomvc-express.bahmutov.com:443/app.css")
```

But this will pass:

```
request("https://todomvc-express.bahmutov.com/app.css")
```

Setting the correct `Host` header (by omitting the port) causes both types of requests to pass.
